newsitem.title: USA: Clinton voices trade concerns to Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: Clinton voices trade concerns to Hashimoto.

text.p: DENVER, June 19 (REUTER) - U.S. President Bill Clinton voiced concern Thursday to Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about Japan's rising trade surplus, U.S. officials said.
In a 70-minute meeting with Hashimoto, Clinton also stressed the importance of Japan promoting domestic demand-led growth and deregulation of its economy.
"He (Clinton) voiced quite specific concerns," White House aide Daniel Tarullo told reporters.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said that Clinton also pointedly reminded Hashimoto that previous persistent Japanese trade surpluses had been a source of "real damage to the bilateral relationship" and said the two nations should not allow trade to become the dominant factor in their ties.
Earlier Thursday, the United States and Japan unveiled a formal consultative process in which they would discuss deregulation of key sectors of Japan's economy.

"The Prime Minister through this agreement has invited the United States to participate in helping Japan formulate dereglation initiatives," U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told reporters.

"Obviously the United States is not going to dictate to Japan what it should do, but we will have a series of negotiations to hammer out measures which we believe Japan should take to deregulate its markets in a manner that both promotes consumer choice and domestic prosperity in Japan and at the same time...provides for increased market access," by the United States and other nations.
Hashimoto has already committed himself to carry out a substantial program of deregulation of the Japanese economy.
"(Today's) initiative does call on the Japanese government to make good on the Prime Minister's promise," Barshefsky said.
She also voiced concern about a recent drop in U.S. car exports to Japan.

"We are concerned by the direction in vehicle sales," she said. But she added that the United States had been encouraged by car parts exports to Japan which have continued to grow at a "healthy" pace.
